questions.prompt: Which metric is most appropriate for measuring conversion rate in an A/B test?
questions.explanation: Conversion rate directly measures the proportion of users who completed the desired action, making it the primary metric for success.

questions.prompt: Why is random assignment of users important in A/B testing?

options.text: To reduce bias and confounding variables

questions.explanation: Random assignment balances both known and unknown factors across groups, minimizing bias.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a statistical significance level (alpha) in A/B testing?

options.text: Defines acceptable probability of Type I error

questions.explanation: Alpha sets the threshold for rejecting the null hypothesis, controlling the chance of a false positive.

questions.prompt: Which scenario indicates a need for a multi-armed bandit approach rather than classic A/B testing?

options.text: Real-time allocation of traffic to the best-performing variant

questions.explanation: Bandits adaptively shift traffic toward the winning variant, improving efficiency in real-time contexts.

questions.prompt: How does the confidence interval help interpret A/B test results?

options.text: Provides range of plausible true effect size

questions.explanation: The CI estimates where the true difference likely falls, giving context to the observed effect.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a common pitfall when running multiple A/B tests simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Multiple simultaneous tests raise the overall probability of a false positive, inflating the Type I error rate.
